learningObjective.title: Discuss the project planning phase and the project lifecycle

questions.question: In IT project planning, which statement best describes rolling wave planning?

options.A: All project work is planned in full detail before any execution begins.
options.B: Near-term work is planned in detail; later work stays high-level and is refined as the project progresses.
options.C: Planning cycles repeat until the final product is achieved, with each cycle replacing the previous plan entirely.
options.D: The schedule is built backward from a fixed go-live date with no further changes allowed.

questions.note:
Rolling wave planning is a **form of progressive elaboration** (PMBOK 6, Sections 6.2.2.2 and 5.1.2.2). Example from a cloud migration: Sprint 1 is fully planned, while Sprint 4 is only defined in terms of goals.
A describes detailed upfront (predictive) planning. C sounds like the iterative approach, which refines the product, not the plan horizon.

questions.question: A project team logs a third-party API delay, an assumption that the cloud service will be available, and a possible security vulnerability in the same document. Which planning tool are they using?
questions.note:
A **RAID Log** tracks **R**isks, **A**ssumptions, **I**ssues and **D**ependencies. Here, the API delay is a current issue, cloud availability is an assumption, and the security vulnerability is a risk (PMBOK 6, Sections 11.2 and 11.5).
A RACI matrix assigns roles, a milestone chart shows key checkpoints, and a burndown chart shows remaining sprint work.

questions.question: According to PMBOK 6 (Section 4.2), which planning document integrates and consolidates all subsidiary plans and baselines?
questions.note:
The **Project Management Plan** is the primary document that ties together all subsidiary plans (scope, schedule, cost, quality, communication, risk, procurement, stakeholder) and baselines.
The Project Charter is an **Initiation** deliverable that authorizes the project. The Scope Management Plan is one of the subsidiary plans, and the Risk Register is a deliverable of the Risk Management Plan.

questions.question: A government portal must meet fixed security compliance requirements, but its UI/UX is expected to evolve with user feedback. Which tailored planning approach fits best?

options.A: Predictive for the whole project, with all scope fixed upfront
options.B: Agile for the whole project, with all planning done in sprints
options.C: Hybrid: predictive for the compliance work, agile for the UI
options.D: No formal planning until the first user feedback arrives

questions.note:
**Hybrid** combines predictive and agile practices when a project has some stable elements and some evolving ones. Fixed compliance suits predictive planning; a changing UI suits agile.
This is an example of **tailoring**: adapting methods to the project's context (PMBOK 6, Section 1.2.4; PMBOK 7 tailoring considerations).

questions.question: An e-commerce platform is released module by module (user login first, then the cart, then payment), and each release gives customers something usable. Which planning approach is this?
questions.note:
**Incremental** delivers completed parts of the product gradually, each delivering customer value, and accepts changes between increments.
The common trap is **Iterative**, which repeats cycles to **refine the same product** until it is final (e.g. tuning a machine learning model). Predictive delivers everything at the end. Kanban is a visual task-tracking tool, not a planning approach.
